name: Girl Child Protection Scheme
full_name: Chief Minister's Girl Child Protection Scheme
summary: A deposit in your daughter's name that she receives when she turns 18, for families with only girl children.
benefit_note: ₹50,000 deposited for a family with one girl child, or ₹25,000 for each of two girl children. Paid out when she turns 18. An annual incentive of ₹1,800 is paid from the sixth year of the deposit.
how_to_apply: Collect your daughter's birth certificate, an income certificate and the sterilisation certificate.
Apply through the Social Welfare Office or the child development office for your area.
The deposit is made in your daughter's name and renewed every five years.
She claims the matured amount when she turns 18.

all.label: Annual family income of ₹1,20,000 or less
all.fix_hint: Income is assessed from your income certificate. If yours is out of date, a fresh one from the e-Sevai centre will reflect your current income.

all.fail_template: Your family income is ₹{user_value}, above the ₹{threshold} limit for this scheme.

all.pass_template: All the children in your family are girls, which is what this scheme is for.

curation_notes: DRAFT — not yet read by a human against the official page. Do not ship.
Taken from the Tamil Nadu Social Welfare Department page on 2026-08-09. Every source_quote is wording from that page.

SENSITIVE FIELDS. parent_sterilised and parent_sterilisation_age must never be asked in the general profile wizard — only inside this scheme's own flow, with a visible reason and an easy skip. See docs/profile-fields.md.

parent_sterilised and sterilisation-age-limit are deliberately fixable:false. Sterilisation is technically an action a person could take, and this product must never suggest it. fixable answers 'would we tell someone to do this', not 'could they'.

TO CONFIRM: whether the income limit is 'not exceeding' ₹1,20,000 (lte, as written here) or 'below' ₹1,20,000 (lt). The department's marriage assistance page words the same figure as 'should not exceed', so lte is the reasonable reading — but confirm on this scheme's own page.
TO CONFIRM: the documents list. The official page does not give one. The five listed follow from the stated conditions but none is quoted.

TO CONFIRM: the girl must 'appear for 10th standard public examination' according to the page. That reads as a condition on the payout rather than on applying, so it is not written as a rule. Check which it is — if it gates the application, it needs a rule and a child_* field.
benefit_value holds the ₹50,000 single-girl-child figure. A family with two girls gets ₹25,000 each, also ₹50,000 in total, so ranking is unaffected either way.
